name: Molniya + Tundra (HEO comms + early warning)
tagline: HEO 63.4° critical inclination — Russian comms + US warn
description: Highly-eccentric orbit constellations using the 63.4° critical inclination — the inclination at which Earth's J2 perturbation does not rotate the line of apsides, so the orbit's apogee stays locked over the chosen hemisphere. Molniya (12-hour period, 600 × 40,000 km) used by Russia since 1965 for high-latitude civilian + military comms and Oko/Meridian early-warning sensors. Tundra (24-hour period, 25,000 × 35,786 km) used by Sirius XM Satellite Radio and US SBIRS-HEO early-warning satellites.
best_known_for: HEO 63.4° critical inclination — Russian comms + US warn
